text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government will impose stricter controls on industrial zone development by approving only highly feasible projects.
-- Vietnam's trade deficit reached $1.1 billion during the January-May period, despite a substantial rise in exports.
-- A United States Overseas Private Investment Corporation delegation has been in Vietnam this week studying the local investment environment.
-- Government officials expect the European Union to approve a proposal to increase import quotas this year for Vietnamese garments and textiles.
-- Vietnam's population will jump to 82 million by the year 2000 from 75 million now.
-- The country's trade environment and economic situation was discussed at a cabinet meeting earlier this week.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has concluded a visit to four European countries. He arrived back in Hanoi on Thursday.
-- A Thai military delegation headed by Supreme Commander General Mongkol Ampornpisit arrived in Vietnam on Thursday and was welcomed by the Army Chief of General Staff, General Pham Van Tra.
-- A Communist Party delegation from India met politburo member Nguyen Duc Binh on Thursday at the end of a five day visit to Vietnam.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam is participating in a non-official neeting of ASEAN Foreign Ministers in Malaysia to discuss plans for Laos, Cambodia and Burma to join the regional grouping.
